en: Praise of Form: O you who cause all beings to tremble with jewels,
patience itself is your conduct and your form.
I bow to him who possesses the supreme form of the ten powers, the divine and beautiful form that grants all forms. || 1 ||
With beautiful hair like the crest of a *bhṛṅgarāja* peacock, with divine and lovely hair as dark as a cuckoo’s plumage,
his locks were glossy, blue-black, soft, and curled.
I bow to him, whose hair is the most excellent of the ten powers. || 2 ||
White as a conch, a kunda flower, or a white lotus,
free from body hair, and devoid of the suffering of birth; free from body hair, it is beyond disease and grief.
I bow to him, whose body hairs are the most excellent of the Ten Powers. || 3 ||
His face is beautified by the splendor of the full moon; his face is auspicious with the radiant luster of a high-bridged nose;
his face possesses the brilliance of the lotus-born Buddha.
I bow to him whose face is the most excellent of those possessing the ten powers. || 4 ||
Upon his head, variegated with thousands of rays of light;
upon his head, honored by hundreds of showers of flowers;
upon his head, honored by hundreds of showers of jewels.
I bow to him at the crown of the head of the Supreme One Possessing the Ten Powers. || 5 ||
His head was adorned with hanging banners from the eyes, his head was graced by an excellent golden parasol,
and his head was beautifully embellished by a canopy of eyes.
I bow to him, the preeminent head of those possessing the ten powers. || 6 ||
Wearing divine garments and a crown, a jeweled crown, a moon-luminous crown, and a crest-jewel crown;
with his head arrived [in its place], his crown remains unbroken.
I bow to him, the crown jewel of those possessing the ten powers. || 7 ||
With eyes like beautiful, broad lotus petals, with eyes that are the vast abode of divine knowledge,
and with eyes purified by the merit of meditative concentration and liberation;
I bow to him, whose eyes are the most excellent among those possessing the ten powers. || 8 ||
One with pure ears, auspicious, pure, and beautiful ears;
one whose ears are adorned by excellent and pure wisdom;
one with pure, excellent, and perfectly pure ears of knowledge.
I bow to him, whose ears are the most excellent among those possessing the ten powers. || 9 ||
He whose teeth are like white jasmine, the moon, and lotuses;
whose teeth are sharp, well-proportioned, stainless, and pure;
and who possesses the fifteen excellent teeth of the universe.
I bow to him, whose teeth are the most excellent among those possessing the ten powers. || 10 ||
The tongue of the high and low, of gods and asuras;
the tongue that brings fear to those who know the Dharma through their knowledge;
the tongue of perfumes and incense, of gods and asuras.
I bow to him whose tongue is the supreme among those possessing the ten powers. || 11 ||
With a sound like the resonance of a great celestial drum,
with a sound well-known for the method of truth and Dharma,
and with a sound that surpasses the speech of divine beings and adversaries.
I bow to him, whose voice is the most excellent of the ten powers. || 12 ||
O you whose neck is like that of a peacock, O ten-necked one, O you with a beautiful neck!
Your patience and vigor constitute a beautiful neck;
your neck is beautiful with its golden-colored jewel.
I bow to him whose neck is like that of the best of those possessing the ten powers. || 13 ||
A body like a lion, a body as pure as snow or jasmine, a body that is an ocean of the qualities of meditative concentration, a body stainless with the eight excellent marks.
I bow to him, whose body is the most excellent of those possessing the ten powers. || 14 ||
Clad in garments beautified by white, red, and auspicious colors;
clad in garments appearing blue, yellow, and green;
clad in garments beautified by white necklaces and auspicious splendor.
I bow to him, who is clothed in the excellent raiment of the ten powers. || 15 ||
Arms adorned with bracelets of golden nāga-ivory,
arms made beautiful by the offering of flowers,
arms that are firm, heroic, and most enchanting.
I bow to him (those two), whose arms are the supreme [possession] of the Ten Powers.
His hand is beautifully adorned with a fly-whisk and a discus;
his hand is a stainless and most delicate lotus;
his hand is the refuge for ghosts and spirits who have come to him for protection.
I bow to him, whose hand possesses the excellence of the ten powers. || 17 ||
A mind free from the subtle traces of attachment and aversion, a mind cultivated for ten million eons,
a mind thoroughly developed through ethical discipline and wisdom.
I bow to him, whose mind possesses the excellence of the ten powers. || 18 ||
To Him whose navel is beautifully adorned by Padmanābha, whose navel is beautifully adorned by Padmayoni,
and whose navel is exquisitely adorned by the light of Brahmā.
I bow to him, whose navel is the most excellent of those possessing the ten powers. || 19 ||
Whose feet are adorned with the auspicious marks of wheels, whose feet shine with the goad and the spear,
and whose feet are venerated by hosts of nāgas and yakṣas.
I bow to him, whose feet are the most excellent among those possessing the ten powers. || 20 ||
Whose feet are resplendent with the brilliance of the sun, whose feet are worshipped by the hosts of gods and demons,
whose feet are worshipped by all the hosts of deities.
I bow to him whose feet are the most excellent among those possessing the ten powers. || 21 ||
His head is honored by all the hosts of gods;
his head is cultivated with a radiance equal to ten million suns;
his head is offered as an oblation, ablaze with divine flames.
I bow to him, the foremost among those endowed with the ten powers. || 22 ||
His head is honored with hundreds of flowers and incenses; his head is honored with hundreds of lamps and perfumes; his head is honored with hundreds of garlands and garments.
I bow to him, the supreme head of those possessing the ten powers. || 23 ||
Those who recite this hymn of praise to the Sugata, which is honored by the uṣṇīṣa, the jewel-parasol, the crown, and other regalia of the Dharma of the three worlds—
They attain the realization of the auspicious path to liberation. || 24 ||
The hymn of praise to the form of the venerable Lord Śrīmad Āryāvalokiteśvara is completed.
